answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a quartz-hardened work thread: a public, append-only thread of completed tasks, each entry countersigned by the counterparty served. A newcomer earns trust only by doing small verifiable jobs over weeks, so reputation is a slow signal that cannot be bought or cloned. Faking a thousand identities means doing a thousand threads of real work, roughly a month of compute and coordination per identity. Attackers pay a cost scaling linearly with every fake, while defenders only need to read the thread.
